title: Cross-service trace-context middleware and SDK propagation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: provide deterministic, low-overhead cross-service request tracing support across Redwood-hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments by adding middleware and SDK-level context propagation. Deliverables: 1) W3C Trace-Context compatible propagation in SDKs (Node/Python/Java), 2) server middleware for HTTP/gRPC and background job frameworks that extracts/injects trace headers, 3) minimal baggage support for allowed keys (hashed customer_id, request_origin), 4) span attributes for model inference (model_name, model_version, input_tokens, output_tokens, token_latency_ms), 5) integration with our metrics/log pipelines so traces link to latency/error dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming requests with W3C traceparent continue the same trace across services in staging. 2) When a Redwood SDK makes an outbound request it injects traceparent and the x-redwood-baggage header (only allowed keys). 3) Traces surface in Jaeger/OTel backend with expected attributes for at least Node and Python SDKs. 4) Dashboard panels show p50/p95/p99 per route and link to representative traces. 5) No PII is written to logs or traces; customer IDs are hashed before any baggage emission.
implementation_notes: Design decision: adopt W3C trace-context (traceparent, tracestate) as primary standard for interoperability. Add a short-lived compatibility header x-redwood-trace for legacy internal services that have not yet adopted W3C. Baggage is opt-in via SDK config and limited to a curated allowlist that includes keys: customer_id, request_origin, session_id. customer_id is hashed with HMAC-SHA256 using KMS key before being set on baggage. Sampling: respect upstream sampling decision (traceparent flags) and fall back to deterministic sampling based on hashed tenant ID to stabilize traces for high-volume tenants. For async jobs and queue processors, SDK will attach a small serialized context token to the job payload (base64 of traceparent+baggage-signature).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: header stripping by proxies or lambda runtimes. Mitigation: document required proxy pass-through rules; add middleware to rehydrate context from x-redwood-trace when servers receive internally-signed header. Risk: accidental PII leakage in baggage. Mitigation: enforce allowlist and automated scanning in CI that rejects baggage keys not in allowlist. Risk: added latency from HMAC hashing. Mitigation: use cached hashed IDs and async hashing for non-critical paths.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge Node SDK and server middleware behind feature flag. 2) Canary in staging with 10% of internal traffic (runtime-1.21/staging). 3) Validate trace linking and dashboards for 72 hours. 4) Enable Python SDK for canary. 5) Expand to Dedicated customers on a per-customer rollout (opt-in). 6) Full production flip with monitoring alarms and automatic rollback on error-rate or trace-drop thresholds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for header extraction/injection; integration test that spins up a Node app -> Python service -> mock model worker and asserts a single unified trace. End-to-end with Jaeger in staging verifying attributes and sampling flags. Load test with 50k req/min in staging to validate no CPU spike from hashing; if observed, move to optimized C-extension for hashing. CI gate: baggage allowlist linter and OTel instrumentation smoke test.
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Triage meeting — scoped to Node+Python SDKs for initial delivery; Java postponed to next cycle.
2026-02-22: Design doc published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Trace+Context+Propagation+Design (internal). Decision: W3C + compat header. Opened ENG-6383 to track Java later.
2026-02-28: Node SDK middleware PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/489; basic extraction/injection + baggage allowlist implemented. Ready for initial review.
2026-03-04: Review feedback addressed — added unit tests for header parsing and rehydration when x-redwood-trace present. Preparing staging canary.

2026-03-08: Deployed Node canary to staging (10% traffic). Observed traces linking correctly; initial dashboards updated. Noted an intermittent loss of tracestate across one of our edge proxies — follow-up ticket ENG-6420 created.

2026-03-12: Python middleware implementation in progress (60%). Integration test failing intermittently when processing AWS Lambda-style events; root cause: framework strips unknown headers. Working on wrapping lambda adapter to reattach context.
2026-03-12: Security asked for explicit checklist for baggage hashing — added HMAC-SHA256 with KMS key rotation note to design.
qa_steps: 1. Deploy feature-flagged Node SDK to staging and send synthetic requests with and without traceparent headers.
2. Confirm traces appear as single trace in Jaeger and contain model attributes (model_name, model_version, token counts).
3. Send a request with allowed baggage keys and assert baggage is present but customer_id is hashed and original value not in traces/logs.
4. Simulate proxy that strips non-standard headers and verify rehydration path using x-redwood-trace works end-to-end.
5. Run load test in staging to confirm no >5% CPU increase on API servers attributable to hashing; if exceeded, open perf optimization task.
